# What compiles

The method names are read out of `src/frontend_native_graph.coil`'s own dispatch tables,
and every cell comes from compiling a real program through the frontend, the verifier,
instruction selection and register allocation. Nothing here is hand-maintained: add a
method to the frontend and a row appears.

**A METHOD IS NOT WHAT COMPILES -- A PROGRAM IS.** The four columns are four ways a real
program uses a result, and they disagree constantly: `substring` compiles when its result
is converted and fails when the same result reaches arithmetic. Reading only one column
gives an answer that is wrong in one direction or the other, which is what the first two
drafts of this report did.

Columns: `converted` = `String(r).length`; `compared` = `r === undefined`;
`in arithmetic` = `n + r`; `then indexed` = call it, then read `v[0]`.

READ A COLUMN THAT FAILS EVERYWHERE AS BEING ABOUT THE COLUMN. If every method fails
under one shape, the shape is what is unsupported -- indexing a string, say -- and no
individual method is implicated. The rows that matter are the ones that DISAGREE with
their neighbours in the same column.

**`compiles` is not `correct`.** This is the ceiling, not the floor -- correctness is
decided in `tests/native-execution-test.coil`, which links a binary and runs it against
node, and which covers a handful of these rows. A row that says `compiles` has never
necessarily produced a right answer.
